simple.meaning: מַאֲכֶלֶת (maʼăkeleth) is a Hebrew object word meaning “something to eat with, i.e. a knife.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 22:6. The surrounding context includes family line, offering, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַאֲכֶלֶת (H3979) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מַאֲכֶלֶת (maʼăkeleth) / H3979 is traced through Genesis 22:6, Genesis 22:10, Judges 19:29, Proverbs 30:14 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.short: something to eat with, i.e. a knife
definitions.full: H3979. maakeleth מַאֲכֶ֫לֶת noun feminine knife (as cutting instrum., or instrument for dividing, making small, compare S[iegfrom] ThLZ.Nov.17. '88 ) Judg 19:29 ; מַאֲכֶ֑לֶת Gen 22:6 , 10 , plural מַאֲכָלוֺת Prov 30:14 .

occurrences.englishText: Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son. He took in his hand the fire and the knife. They both went together.
Abraham stretched out his hand, and took the knife to kill his son.
When he had come into his house, he took a knife and cut up his concubine, and divided her, limb by limb, into twelve pieces, and sent her throughout all the borders of Israel.
There is a generation whose teeth are like swords,
